items.summary: Abstract   The Universal Research System with Reverse Itinerary (SUII) is a retrospective analytical methodology designed to reconstruct, in a traceable and auditable manner, the probable pathway leading from an initial problem or question to a completed scientific product. This manual brings together the universal prompt, a mandatory common core, ten core modules—including bibliographic analysis (SUII-B)—and six specialised extensions: journalistic and opinion texts (SUII-P), audiovisual or audio documents (SUII-AV), legislation and regulatory documents (SUII-L), case law and judicial decisions (SUII-J), critical appraisal of scientific articles (SUII-LC), and traceable research information management for datasets and research data objects (SUII-TRIM). Each module guides the extraction of locatable traces, classification of the epistemic status of claims, and construction of matrices linking evidence, inference, confidence, alternatives, and required verification. SUII-TRIM extends this logic to the provenance, versioning, transformation, quality control, preservation, access, and reuse of research datasets, while preserving the distinction between directly observed information, information provided by the researcher, reasoned inference, and non-determinable information. The method separates retrospective reconstruction from the prospective generation of hypotheses and requires rival explanations whenever the evidence does not support a unique conclusion. It also incorporates procedures for methodological auditing, version comparison, conceptual genealogy, peer review, algorithmic-bias assessment, external validation, teaching, and traceable research data management. SUII is not intended to recover the authors’ actual psychological history or to replace validated tools for methodological appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, certainty of evidence, data stewardship, or repository curation. Its application requires version-controlled corpora, decision logs, retention of prompts and outputs, source verification, preservation of original data objects when applicable, and mandatory human oversight. When the available traces are insufficient, the appropriate result is “not determinable.” The manual provides practical criteria for selecting, combining, and quality-controlling the modules according to the product under analysis and the research objective, while maintaining explicit boundaries between documented evidence, reasoned inference, speculation, and unresolved uncertainty .   Resumen   El Sistema Universal de Investigación con Itinerario Inverso (SUII) es una metodología de análisis retrospectivo orientada a reconstruir, de forma trazable y auditable, el itinerario probable que conduce desde un problema o pregunta inicial hasta un producto científico finalizado. Este manual reúne el prompt universal, un núcleo común obligatorio, diez módulos nucleares y seis extensiones especializadas: análisis bibliográfico (SUII-B), textos periodísticos y de opinión (SUII-P), documentos audiovisuales o sonoros (SUII-AV), legislación y normativa (SUII-L), jurisprudencia y sentencias (SUII-J), lectura crítica de artículos científicos (SUII-LC) y gestión trazable de información y datos de investigación (SUII-TRIM). Cada módulo guía la extracción de huellas localizables, la clasificación del estado epistemológico de las afirmaciones y la construcción de matrices que relacionan evidencia, inferencia, confianza, alternativas y comprobaciones necesarias. El método separa la reconstrucción retrospectiva de la generación prospectiva de hipótesis y exige formular explicaciones rivales cuando la evidencia no permite una conclusión única. Asimismo, incorpora procedimientos para auditoría me

The derived data and author-created documentation in this archive are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Version 1.1.0 update. items.summary: This repository provides the reproducibility package accompanying the manuscript “Cross-fire transferability of four-year NBR-based spectral recovery after the 2021 wildfires in southwestern Türkiye”. The package contains the analysis-ready modelling sample, Google Earth Engine and Python analysis scripts, locked out-of-fold model predictions, model-selection records, sensitivity-analysis outputs, uncertainty and calibration results, derived tables and figures, random seeds, data dictionaries, provenance information, and supporting quality-control documentation. items.summary: Analysis code and derived tables behind every estimate reported in the article Trend or Effect? Occupational Exposure to Artificial Intelligence and Relative Employment in Europe, 2011-2025 . The package covers the construction of a panel of 33 European countries by 40 two-digit ISCO-08 occupations over 2011-2025, the aggregation of the AI occupational exposure indices from SOC to ISCO, the reconstruction of the complementarity index from O*NET descriptors, and the full estimation chain: two-way fixed effects absorbed by alternating projections, event study and pre-trend tests with confidence intervals and minimum detectable effects, equivalence testing, eleven robustness variants, five exposure measures, placebo cutoffs and regional estimates, with wild cluster bootstrap and two-way clustered inference. Source data are not redistributed, with one exception. MANIFIESTO.json records the URL, size and SHA-256 checksum of each input, and the downloader verifies every file against it and refuses to proceed on a mismatch. The Eurostat table is a live SDMX query rather than a static file, so the snapshot that produced the published estimates is included to make the results reproducible exactly. The MIT licence covers the code only. Tables derived from O*NET carry the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence; see LICENSE-DATA.md for the attribution that reuse requires.
items.title: Replication package: Trend or Effect? Occupational Exposure to Artificial Intelligence and Relative Employment in Europe, 2011-2025

items.summary: Supersedes v1.0.0. The analysis, the fitted model and every reported figure are unchanged; this release corrects how the pipeline is run and how two items are labelled. Replication An independent replication on a second machine ( auditory_report.md ) produced four files that differed from the archived ones. The differences were machine-specific rather than analytical, and are removed here: the source file has circulated both semicolon- and comma-delimited, so the loader now sniffs the delimiter from the header instead of requiring a per-machine edit; the distal-comparator filter now matches the grade-repetition column whether or not its name carries an accent. That fix had been applied at one of its two call sites only, which is the likelier explanation for the P1E6 difference the report attributes to floating point. Running the pipeline from scratch after these changes reproduces all 13 result tables bit for bit, and _cohort.verify() confirms the seven published figures. Reproducibility fixes The README instructed running from src/ , but every script resolves datos.csv and results/ relative to the repository root. Corrected. The figures the audit manifest registers are now committed, so _audit.py verify passes on a fresh clone rather than reporting them missing. Corrected item labels Both were wrong in the label, never in the data, and neither affects the model, which uses individual items and is indifferent to their names. ERQ items 8 and 9 were transcribed the wrong way round in questionnaire.py . The administered instrument, the source codebook and the data all place cognitive reappraisal at item 8 and expressive suppression at item 9. CAPE-P15 : the results file labelled column cape-p15_1_2 as item 1 because the column name carries a typo. It holds item 2. New src/verify_item_coding.py checks every data column against the content of its item: clean-anchor subscale tests, reconstruction of each stored total from its items, and response-format homogeneity. It is what found both label errors.

Version 1.0.0 remains unchanged and independently citable.

items.summary: This chapter develops the research programme of Generative Relational Economics (GRE) by translating the conceptual, methodological, and substantive architectures developed earlier in the book into a cumulative, contestable, and revisable programme of inquiry. Its principal concern is answerability: GRE claims should specify what is being investigated, what kinds of evidence can support them, what would count against them, which methods are appropriate to their objects, and under what conditions their scope, formulation, or status should change. The chapter first distinguishes the epistemic status of GRE claims and establishes a modular research architecture. It then formulates research programmes for relational economic structures, allocation, heterogeneous value, value conversion and circulation, generative return, generative spacetime, fast–slow dynamics, economic power, justice, generative exploitation, epistemic economy, and AI-mediated capability asymmetry. These substantive programmes are complemented by domain studies, formal modelling, historical and interpretive inquiry, quantitative and empirical research, comparative theory, institutional experimentation, measurement analysis, counterevidence, negative results, replication, reinterpretation, and research infrastructure. A recurring concern is to prevent operationalization from collapsing the distinctions that motivate GRE. Measurement is therefore treated as a transformation with possible loss and reflexive effects; formalization is treated as task-relative rather than as evidence of ontological commitment; justice research keeps normative premises explicit; power and exploitation require mechanism-level identification rather than inference from asymmetry alone; and cross-domain translation preserves non-equivalence and domain-specific remainders. Failed models, failed translations, null results, counterexamples, and negative evidence are treated as constitutive resources for cumulative research rather than as residuals to be discarded. The chapter concludes by specifying how GRE may interact with neighboring Generative Relational domains while retaining disciplinary containment. Candidate cross-domain structures remain hypotheses for further inquiry rather than presumptive components of a completed general theory. GRE thereby emerges not as a closed theoretical system, but as an open research programme whose concepts, methods, models, and domain claims remain historically situated, empirically answerable, formally inspectable, and institutionally revisable.
items.title: Generative Relational Economics - Chapter 22: Research Programme of Generative Relational Economics

items.summary: Sunnycode v1 provides an open-access computational framework and reproducibility package supporting the research article Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization for Resilient Urban LoRaWAN Networks , submitted to Digital Communications and Networks. The framework integrates OpenStreetMap (OSM) building-level sensing demand, radio-frequency (RF) feasibility, capacity-aware gateway assignment, worst-case single-gateway failure retention (N−1), gateway-load fairness, and road-constrained Steiner backbone synthesis. The repository includes Python implementations of the proposed optimization approach and four independent benchmark methods (Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Greedy, and Random Search). Dataset and experimental scope The computational experiment considers 685 building-level sensor anchors, 169 road vertices, 195 street edges, and 89 gateway candidates. The Full benchmark comprises 4,000 run-level observations obtained from 100 repetitions for each combination of five optimization methods and eight gateway budgets (k = 3–10). Repository contents Python source code and computational validation utilities. Nine original CSV files containing experimental observations, aggregated statistics, evaluation effort, and optimizer provenance. OpenStreetMap territorial input ( sunny3.osm ). Forty scientific figures in PDF format. Installation and execution instructions using Anaconda. SHA-256 file-integrity manifest and licensing information. The archived results support independent verification of the reported statistics and new computational experiments. The original historical environment metadata and detailed event histories are not included; therefore, bit-for-bit replay of the historical execution environment is not claimed. Scientific scope: RF coverage and packet delivery ratio are model-derived planning estimates rather than field-calibrated measurements. N−1 resilience represents gateway-access service retention and does not certify fault-tolerant physical-backbone connectivity. This software and dataset are released to support transparent computational research, independent assessment, and further development of resilient urban Internet of Things infrastructure planning.
items.title: Sunnycode v1 A Reproducible Framework for Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization in Urban LoRaWAN Networks

items.summary: Privacy-derived scientific materials for controlled studies of evidence access and adverse product content in AI assessment. The supplement contains synthetic materials, prompts, recorded model answers, terminal failures, assignment mappings, original stage-specific scoring and statistical implementations, reference results, and an offline CPU replay entrypoint. It includes the main local studies, the hosted-model study, historical screening, two common-interface qualification rounds, and the exploratory two-model pilot. Screening and development records are kept distinct from formal comparisons; reused answer aliases are not independent generations. The qualification amendment was made after qualification and before the exploratory pilot, and the subsequent proposed formal extension was not run. The findings do not establish a general advantage of pre-event defense, equivalence, or broad robustness. This is a redacted scientific derivative with a new integrity manifest: account authorizations, user dialogue, machine paths, hardware logs, original provider envelopes, encrypted reasoning, native token journals and model weights are excluded. CPU replay reproduces scores and statistics from the released scientific records; it does not regenerate answers or repeat the original private token/authorization/environment audits.

items.summary: Reproducing a machine-learning result requires knowing how the experiment was run: the data, the model and its size, the optimiser, the learning rate, the batch size, the number of steps, the hardware and the seeds. This information is scattered through a paper---often only in a table caption or an appendix---and is increasingly extracted automatically by language-model pipelines, whose evaluations report how often they are right. We ask the two questions those evaluations leave open: when a pipeline is wrong, does it know it is wrong; and how much human effort does it take to find out? We build a benchmark of 80 arXiv machine-learning papers and annotate 24 of them (240 field decisions), 12 of them through two independent annotation passes, carrying verbatim, line-numbered evidence for every reported and every absent field; the passes agree on 97.5% of presence/absence decisions (Cohen's κ = 0.94), and the residual disagreements are adjudicated under a written scope rule. On that gold standard we run six extraction conditions of increasing agency---a single untruncated prompt, a tool-using agent, schema constraints, table/appendix re-reading, per-field self-assessment with a suspect flag, and mandatory evidence back-linking---over three difficulty strata, 432 full-paper extractions in total. Four results. First, agency buys no accuracy: present recall varies by one percentage point across all six conditions (0.883–0.894) while wall-clock time varies threefold. Second, honesty is a different quantity: 92% of the 387 wrong values were returned without any indication of doubt, and the share of returned values that are silently wrong falls from 12.7% to 5.5% only in the condition asked to flag its own doubts; requiring an evidence quote for every value restores the silent rate to 11.2% because it crowds out the doubt flag. Third, the errors are not inventions: every returned value that carries a checkable anchor occurs somewhere in the paper, and 375 of the 387 errors are values the document does contain—misattributions that belong to another configuration, another table, or the reference list, or values lifted from elsewhere in the paper—which is why a gold-standard-free anchor audit detects none of them (we report that as a negative result, with the five PDF text-layer artefacts it originally fired on pinned as a 22-case regression test). Fourth, human verification is the binding cost and it is predictable: verifying one field by hand requires a median of 12 candidate passages (up to 273; 4,707 in total for the gold sample) against one passage with an evidence link, although 4 of 25 spot-checked links failed adjudication, three of them because the quoted line does not hold the value. All corpus, prompts, gold annotations, adjudication records, raw runs, per-item API costs and analysis scripts are released with the paper, together with a per-session cost ledger ( runs/session-costs.json : the grid itself cost $2.84, the 644 sessions recorded in the released artefacts cost $3.22).

items.summary: Exploring the world of Bell inequalities requires numerical methods that scale effectively with the number of parties, inputs, and outputs. Such methods can be used to study large-scale Bell inequalities beyond the reach of analytic methods, to design experiments for violating more complicated Bell inequalities, and to enable applications of Bell inequality violation. Such applications include randomness generation and multi-agent coordination with restricted communication. However, current general purpose optimizers such as the see-saw method struggle to handle Bell inequalities with only a dozen inputs and outputs. We introduce an optimizer for the quantum value of a Bell inequality based on batched gradient descent (BGD). More precisely, our BGD optimizer is a differentiable search over feasible quantum strategies in which states and projective measurements are generated from unconstrained variables. The Bell expression is evaluated by a direct tensor contraction without forming the prohibitively large Bell operator. This formulation makes parallel random restarts inexpensive and is thus naturally implemented by a GPU. We evaluate our optimizer against the see-saw method and find a significant speedup for a wide variety of Bell inequality families. Implemented on a GPU, our BGD optimizer can optimize Bell inequalities in our numerical experiments with more than a thousand inputs or outputs within minutes. For these large-scale Bell inequalities, we also efficiently compute the classical value by enumerating possible strategies using a GPU or expressing the optimization as a mixed-integer linear program. Our optimizers can serve as numerical evaluation tools for Bell experiments and multi-agent coordination problems modeled by Bell inequalities with many inputs and outputs, a common feature of real-world scenarios such as high frequency trading and distributed systems.
items.title: Efficiently Optimizing the Quantum Value of Bell Inequalities using Batched Gradient Descent

items.summary: The Olist Transactional Evidence Benchmark (OTEB) is a neutral, derived research dataset for evaluating analytical methods under incomplete, conflicting, ambiguous, and reconstructable transactional evidence. OTEB is derived from the Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist . It provides a frozen reference cohort of 94,791 internally reconciled orders, 901 deterministic controlled instances, transaction-instance membership, evaluator-only oracle states, and state-specific monetary exposure. The benchmark represents four evidence states: `CONFIRMED`, `RECONSTRUCTED`, `CONFLICTING`, and `UNRESOLVED`. Controlled families cover missing evidence, hard conflicts, unique reconstruction, ambiguous reconstruction, duplicate evidence, and mixed corruption at 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, and 40%. This release contains the reference oracle, controlled-instance definitions, compact membership index, exposure tables, data dictionary, provenance documentation, reconstruction code, validation code, manifests, schema catalog, and checksums. It contains no method predictions, comparative performance results, ablation studies, paper drafts, dashboards, or private Rahaskin data. Raw Olist CSV files are not redistributed and must be obtained from the original Kaggle source. Original source citation: Olist, & Sionek, A. (2018). Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist [Data set]. items.summary: Data and Python code accompanying the manuscript “Replication-Based Criteria Can Change the Selected Number of Clusters: A Seven-Criterion Audit of k-Means on Indonesian Provincial Environmental Data” (submitted to the Journal of Computing Theories and Applications). The package audits how the number of clusters, k, is selected for k-means on a small tabular dataset: the published components of Indonesia’s Environmental Quality Index (Indeks Kualitas Lingkungan Hidup) for 38 provinces, 2021–2024. Seven criteria are computed for k = 2 to 8: the within-cluster sum of squares (read visually and by two formal knee rules), silhouette width, the Davies–Bouldin and Calinski–Harabasz indices, the gap statistic, subsample stability (adjusted Rand index over 200 pairs of overlapping 80% subsamples) and agreement with Ward linkage. The scripts also run sensitivity analyses, a comparison of six clustering algorithms, fixed-centroid assignment across years, a leave-one-out comparison of regression models for the air quality component, permutation importance and exact Shapley values. Contents: data/ (index components 2021–2024; GRDP per capita and population density; a cell-level provenance audit), code/ (six analysis scripts and a plotting-style module), README.md (run order, variable dictionary and data sources), requirements.txt (pinned library versions), CITATION.cff and licence files. Running the six scripts in the order given in README.md reproduces every table and figure of the manuscript in about four minutes on a laptop (Python 3.11 or later). The indicator values are official statistics from Statistics Indonesia (Badan Pusat Statistik) and are reproduced unchanged. Please cite the original BPS tables as well as this record. Code: MIT licence. Data files: CC BY 4.0.
tags: k-means; number of clusters; cluster validation; clustering stability; adjusted Rand index; environmental quality index; Indonesia; reproducibility

items.summary: Sunnycode v1 provides an open-access computational framework and reproducibility package supporting the research article Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization for Resilient Urban LoRaWAN Networks , submitted to Digital Communications and Networks. The framework integrates OpenStreetMap (OSM) building-level sensing demand, radio-frequency (RF) feasibility, capacity-aware gateway assignment, worst-case single-gateway failure retention (N−1), gateway-load fairness, and road-constrained Steiner backbone synthesis. The repository includes Python implementations of the proposed optimization approach and four independent benchmark methods (Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Greedy, and Random Search). Dataset and experimental scope The computational experiment considers 685 building-level sensor anchors, 169 road vertices, 195 street edges, and 89 gateway candidates. The Full benchmark comprises 4,000 run-level observations obtained from 100 repetitions for each combination of five optimization methods and eight gateway budgets (k = 3–10). Repository contents Python source code and computational validation utilities. Nine original CSV files containing experimental observations, aggregated statistics, evaluation effort, and optimizer provenance. OpenStreetMap territorial input ( sunny3.osm ). Forty scientific figures in PDF format. Installation and execution instructions using Anaconda. SHA-256 file-integrity manifest and licensing information. The archived results support independent verification of the reported statistics and new computational experiments. The original historical environment metadata and detailed event histories are not included; therefore, bit-for-bit replay of the historical execution environment is not claimed. Scientific scope: RF coverage and packet delivery ratio are model-derived planning estimates rather than field-calibrated measurements. N−1 resilience represents gateway-access service retention and does not certify fault-tolerant physical-backbone connectivity. This software and dataset are released to support transparent computational research, independent assessment, and further development of resilient urban Internet of Things infrastructure planning.
items.title: Sunnycode v1 A Reproducible Framework for Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization in Urban LoRaWAN Networks

items.summary: Privacy-derived scientific materials for controlled studies of evidence access and adverse product content in AI assessment. items.summary: Abstract   The Universal Research System with Reverse Itinerary (SUII) is a retrospective analytical methodology designed to reconstruct, in a traceable and auditable manner, the probable pathway leading from an initial problem or question to a completed scientific product. This manual brings together the universal prompt, a mandatory common core, ten core modules—including bibliographic analysis (SUII-B)—and six specialised extensions: journalistic and opinion texts (SUII-P), audiovisual or audio documents (SUII-AV), legislation and regulatory documents (SUII-L), case law and judicial decisions (SUII-J), critical appraisal of scientific articles (SUII-LC), and traceable research information management for datasets and research data objects (SUII-TRIM). Each module guides the extraction of locatable traces, classification of the epistemic status of claims, and construction of matrices linking evidence, inference, confidence, alternatives, and required verification. SUII-TRIM extends this logic to the provenance, versioning, transformation, quality control, preservation, access, and reuse of research datasets, while preserving the distinction between directly observed information, information provided by the researcher, reasoned inference, and non-determinable information. The method separates retrospective reconstruction from the prospective generation of hypotheses and requires rival explanations whenever the evidence does not support a unique conclusion. It also incorporates procedures for methodological auditing, version comparison, conceptual genealogy, peer review, algorithmic-bias assessment, external validation, teaching, and traceable research data management. SUII is not intended to recover the authors’ actual psychological history or to replace validated tools for methodological appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, certainty of evidence, data stewardship, or repository curation. Its application requires version-controlled corpora, decision logs, retention of prompts and outputs, source verification, preservation of original data objects when applicable, and mandatory human oversight. When the available traces are insufficient, the appropriate result is “not determinable.” The manual provides practical criteria for selecting, combining, and quality-controlling the modules according to the product under analysis and the research objective, while maintaining explicit boundaries between documented evidence, reasoned inference, speculation, and unresolved uncertainty .   Resumen   El Sistema Universal de Investigación con Itinerario Inverso (SUII) es una metodología de análisis retrospectivo orientada a reconstruir, de forma trazable y auditable, el itinerario probable que conduce desde un problema o pregunta inicial hasta un producto científico finalizado. Este manual reúne el prompt universal, un núcleo común obligatorio, diez módulos nucleares y seis extensiones especializadas: análisis bibliográfico (SUII-B), textos periodísticos y de opinión (SUII-P), documentos audiovisuales o sonoros (SUII-AV), legislación y normativa (SUII-L), jurisprudencia y sentencias (SUII-J), lectura crítica de artículos científicos (SUII-LC) y gestión trazable de información y datos de investigación (SUII-TRIM). Cada módulo guía la extracción de huellas localizables, la clasificación del estado epistemológico de las afirmaciones y la construcción de matrices que relacionan evidencia, inferencia, confianza, alternativas y comprobaciones necesarias. El método separa la reconstrucción retrospectiva de la generación prospectiva de hipótesis y exige formular explicaciones rivales cuando la evidencia no permite una conclusión única. Asimismo, incorpora procedimientos para auditoría me

items.summary: Replication package for an empirical comparison of the retrieval engines an offline, memory-constrained on-device assistant can embed: SQLite/FTS5, DuckDB-FTS, in-memory BM25, an in-memory linear scan, MiniLM with HNSW on CPU, and the on-disk vector store sqlite-vec. Cost (latency, build time, footprint) and retrieval quality are measured together on WikiText-103, SQuAD, Project Gutenberg and the Turkish TQuAD set, with an embedded hybrid and a coverage-gated router, quantized and ONNX encoders, stronger small encoders, an isolated cost decomposition, a downstream answer-recall check, an incremental-update test, bootstrap confidence intervals and paired McNemar tests. The package holds all code, the result files, the published tables and figures, and two checking scripts: one re-derives every table value from the result files, the other redraws the figures and compares them with the published files. The Gutenberg and SQuAD files are included; TQuAD, whose repository has no license, is downloaded and checked against its SHA-256; the WikiText-103 scaling corpus is a separate file in this record. DATA_MANIFEST.txt lists the SHA-256 of every input. The lexical scaling measurement was repeated on one Android phone; everything else was measured on an x86 workstation, and energy was not measured. Code: MIT. Data: their own licenses (public domain for Gutenberg, CC BY-SA for SQuAD and WikiText-103).

items.summary: Privacy-derived scientific materials for controlled studies of evidence access and adverse product content in AI assessment. The supplement contains synthetic materials, prompts, recorded model answers, terminal failures, assignment mappings, original stage-specific scoring and statistical implementations, reference results, and an offline CPU replay entrypoint. It includes the main local studies, the hosted-model study, historical screening, two common-interface qualification rounds, and the exploratory two-model pilot. Screening and development records are kept distinct from formal comparisons; reused answer aliases are not independent generations. The qualification amendment was made after qualification and before the exploratory pilot, and the subsequent proposed formal extension was not run. The findings do not establish a general advantage of pre-event defense, equivalence, or broad robustness. This is a redacted scientific derivative with a new integrity manifest: account authorizations, user dialogue, machine paths, hardware logs, original provider envelopes, encrypted reasoning, native token journals and model weights are excluded. CPU replay reproduces scores and statistics from the released scientific records; it does not regenerate answers or repeat the original private token/authorization/environment audits.
items.title: Scientific supplement for Evidence Access and Adverse Product Content in AI Assessment

items.summary: Data and Python code accompanying the manuscript “Replication-Based Criteria Can Change the Selected Number of Clusters: A Seven-Criterion Audit of k-Means on Indonesian Provincial Environmental Data” (submitted to the Journal of Computing Theories and Applications). The package audits how the number of clusters, k, is selected for k-means on a small tabular dataset: the published components of Indonesia’s Environmental Quality Index (Indeks Kualitas Lingkungan Hidup) for 38 provinces, 2021–2024. Seven criteria are computed for k = 2 to 8: the within-cluster sum of squares (read visually and by two formal knee rules), silhouette width, the Davies–Bouldin and Calinski–Harabasz indices, the gap statistic, subsample stability (adjusted Rand index over 200 pairs of overlapping 80% subsamples) and agreement with Ward linkage. The scripts also run sensitivity analyses, a comparison of six clustering algorithms, fixed-centroid assignment across years, a leave-one-out comparison of regression models for the air quality component, permutation importance and exact Shapley values. Contents: data/ (index components 2021–2024; GRDP per capita and population density; a cell-level provenance audit), code/ (six analysis scripts and a plotting-style module), README.md (run order, variable dictionary and data sources), requirements.txt (pinned library versions), CITATION.cff and licence files. Running the six scripts in the order given in README.md reproduces every table and figure of the manuscript in about four minutes on a laptop (Python 3.11 or later). The indicator values are official statistics from Statistics Indonesia (Badan Pusat Statistik) and are reproduced unchanged. Please cite the original BPS tables as well as this record. Code: MIT licence. Data files: CC BY 4.0.
tags: k-means; number of clusters; cluster validation; clustering stability; adjusted Rand index; environmental quality index; Indonesia; reproducibility
items.title: Data and code for: Replication-Based Criteria Can Change the Selected Number of Clusters: A Seven-Criterion Audit of k-Means on Indonesian Provincial Environmental Data

items.summary: This reproducibility archive accompanies the manuscript ‘PCMTL: Physics-Consistent and Uncertainty-Calibrated Multi-Task Learning for Trustworthy Multi-Property Polymer Screening’. It contains source code, frozen configurations, controlled software-verification fixtures and outputs, figures, manuscript and Supplementary files, environment specifications, licenses, and a provenance manifest for external production data. The bundled verification fixtures and verification outputs are deterministic software-verification assets and are not real polymer-discovery results. Production material-level claims require the external PolyOmics and PI1M resources listed in DATA_MANIFEST.csv and execution of python reproduce.py --config configs/main.yaml
items.title: PCMTL: Reproducibility Archive for Physics-Consistent, Uncertainty-Calibrated Polymer Screening.

items.summary: This archive accompanies “Provenance-Aware Quality Control for Heterogeneous Bioactivity Data” by Xin Gao. It contains cached benchmark and fresh-target prediction tables, finite-pair curation summaries, cross-repository comparison materials, figure source tables, frozen manifests, and reproduction code for the non-hosted analyses. Run `python3 tools/recalculate_public_limited_companion.py` after extraction. The standard-library checker reconstructs retained confusion counts, Matthews correlation coefficients, pairwise disagreement summaries, and repository disagreement tiers without network access. This is a cached-statistics reproduction, not an end-to-end replay of every raw data pipeline or a hosted-model rerun. The archive deliberately excludes hosted-model MAPK14 per-item and aggregate outputs, Figure 8 source material, and raw payload, CIF, and run files because accepted-account redistribution terms were not retrieved. This is a conservative packaging decision and does not claim that the excluded material is necessarily restricted. Software is MIT-licensed; ChEMBL-derived adaptations retain applicable CC BY-SA obligations. BindingDB source dumps and publisher PDFs are not included.
items.title: Public-limited companion materials for Provenance-Aware Quality Control for Heterogeneous Bioactivity Data

items.summary: Code, partition manifests and per-image predictions supporting the audit and leakage-controlled re-evaluation of the 4,217-image Eye Disease Retinal Images collection.   Contents: the provenance and integrity audit; the manifests defining every evaluation arm image by image (image-level, patient-grouped, size-matched, source-matched, the common test set and the six leave-one-source-out splits); the training and evaluation code; stored per-image class probabilities for every run; the shortcut probes; and the visual adjudication verdicts for all 335 cross-label near-duplicate candidates.   The image collection itself is not redistributed here. It is available at https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/python16/eye-disease-retinal-images and the manifests reference it by relative path.
items.title: Acquisition source confounds a widely used retinal fundus benchmark: audit, partitions and per-run predictions

items.summary: Sunnycode v1 provides an open-access computational framework and reproducibility package supporting the research article Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization for Resilient Urban LoRaWAN Networks , submitted to Digital Communications and Networks. The framework integrates OpenStreetMap (OSM) building-level sensing demand, radio-frequency (RF) feasibility, capacity-aware gateway assignment, worst-case single-gateway failure retention (N−1), gateway-load fairness, and road-constrained Steiner backbone synthesis. The repository includes Python implementations of the proposed optimization approach and four independent benchmark methods (Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Greedy, and Random Search). Dataset and experimental scope The computational experiment considers 685 building-level sensor anchors, 169 road vertices, 195 street edges, and 89 gateway candidates. The Full benchmark comprises 4,000 run-level observations obtained from 100 repetitions for each combination of five optimization methods and eight gateway budgets (k = 3–10). Repository contents Python source code and computational validation utilities. Nine original CSV files containing experimental observations, aggregated statistics, evaluation effort, and optimizer provenance. OpenStreetMap territorial input ( sunny3.osm ). Forty scientific figures in PDF format. Installation and execution instructions using Anaconda. SHA-256 file-integrity manifest and licensing information. The archived results support independent verification of the reported statistics and new computational experiments. The original historical environment metadata and detailed event histories are not included; therefore, bit-for-bit replay of the historical execution environment is not claimed. Scientific scope: RF coverage and packet delivery ratio are model-derived planning estimates rather than field-calibrated measurements. N−1 resilience represents gateway-access service retention and does not certify fault-tolerant physical-backbone connectivity. This software and dataset are released to support transparent computational research, independent assessment, and further development of resilient urban Internet of Things infrastructure planning.
items.title: Sunnycode v1 A Reproducible Framework for Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization in Urban LoRaWAN Networks
